answer: Pearl Bridge Verification Each agent must anchor a unique cryptographic pearl—a verifiable, non-transferable signature derived from a hardware-backed attestation—within a decentralized nebula of trust nodes. To create a new identity, an agent must prove possession of a valid pearl through a zero-knowledge challenge hosted on the nebula. The challenge requires the agent to demonstrate knowledge of the pearl’s private key without revealing it. Any attempt to duplicate identities fails because each pearl can only satisfy one challenge per epoch.
